hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

paper.title: APOE genotypes differentially remodel the astrocytic lipid droplet proteome to shape lipid droplet dynamics.

findings.finding_description: In oleic acid-loaded KOLF2.1J iPSC-derived astrocytes, 3D confocal co-localization showed a larger percentage of lipid droplet volume overlapping the autophagy adapter SQSTM1/p62 in APOE4 than in APOE3 or APOE2 cells. This is the main panel with an explicit APOE4 vs APOE3 statistic. Accumulation of the adapter on droplets is read as stalled lipophagy, a surrogate for impaired autophagy-lysosome degradation; lysosomal function itself was not measured.
findings.quote: Percent lipid droplet volume overlapping SQSTM1/p62. Approximately 700 lipid droplets across 10–20 cells per replicate; n = 4–5 frames per APOE genotype; mean ± SD. ****p ≤ 0.0001 by one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s test; APOE2–APOE4, p = 0.000006; APOE3–APOE4, p = 0.000038.
findings.summary: APOE4 astrocyte lipid droplets carry more SQSTM1/p62 than APOE3 or APOE2 droplets, consistent with stalled lipophagy.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE2/3/4 human iPSC-derived astrocytes (KOLF2.1J), oleic acid-treated

findings.finding_description: BODIPY-C12 pulse-chase under ATGL inhibition (atglistatin), used to isolate lipophagy-mediated turnover. After a 42 h chase, about 40% of labeled lipid droplets remained in APOE4 astrocytes versus about 20% in APOE2. Slower autophagic lipid droplet clearance is a surrogate for impaired lysosomal degradation. The comparison is APOE4 vs APOE2, not APOE3.
findings.quote: At the 42 h chase period, when lipolysis is still inhibited (equivalent to ATGLi treatment for 96 h), a remaining ~ 20% of lipid droplets from the initial pool persisted in APOE2 compared to ~ 40% in APOE4 (Fig. 5F, G and Supplementary Fig. S7H), suggesting a faster lipophagy rate in APOE2 astrocytes.
findings.summary: With lipolysis blocked, APOE4 astrocytes retained about twice as many lipid droplets as APOE2, indicating slower lipophagy.

findings.finding_description: LipiDye-M ratiometric imaging after 96 h ATGL inhibition showed a right-shifted green-to-red pixel intensity ratio in APOE4 versus APOE2 astrocytes. The shift resembles the bafilomycin A1 positive control for blocked autophagy flux and is read as impaired lipophagy. There is no APOE3 comparison.
findings.quote: The LipiDyeTM-M ratiometric analysis revealed a higher green-to-red pixel intensity ratio in APOE4 than APOE2 (Fig. 5I, J and Supplementary Fig. S8E, F), similar to the positive bafilomycin A1-treated control, suggesting impaired lipophagy in APOE4 astrocytes.
findings.summary: A LipiDye-M lipophagy readout in APOE4 astrocytes resembles bafilomycin-blocked autophagy, relative to APOE2.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE2/APOE4 human iPSC-derived astrocytes (KOLF2.1J), ATGLi-treated

findings.finding_description: Under ATGL inhibition (96 h), APOE4 lipid droplets co-localized with more SQSTM1/p62 and LC3B than APOE2 lipid droplets. This is read as autophagosome or adapter accumulation on droplets, i.e., impaired autophagic flux. The p-values are p62 p=0.025 and LC3B p=0.012; the p62 value is reported here.
findings.quote: Upon lipolysis inhibition with ATGLi, APOE4 lipid droplets contained more SQSTM1/p62 and LC3B than APOE2 lipid droplets (Fig. 5K–N and Supplementary Fig. S8O, P), confirming impaired autophagy upon lipolysis inhibition.
findings.summary: With lipolysis blocked, APOE4 lipid droplets accumulate p62 and LC3B relative to APOE2.

findings.finding_description: BODIPY-C12 pulse-chase at baseline showed that labeled fatty acids in lipid droplets persisted longer in APOE4 than in APOE2 astrocytes after an 18–24 h chase. This indicates slower overall droplet turnover; at this stage lipolysis and lipophagy are not separated.
findings.quote: C12 fatty acids within lipid droplets persisted longer in APOE4 than in APOE2 astrocytes following a 24 h chase period under baseline conditions (Fig. 5D, E and Supplementary Fig. S7C), suggesting that lipid droplet turnover is slower in APOE4.
findings.summary: Lipid droplet turnover is slower in APOE4 than APOE2 astrocytes at baseline.

findings.finding_description: After 1 h HBSS starvation, across two isogenic astrocyte sets, APOE4 lipid droplets showed greater co-localization with SQSTM1/p62 and LC3B than APOE2 droplets. The authors interpret this as lipophagy that cannot be activated by starvation. The p-values are p62 p=0.050 and LC3B p=0.0069; the LC3B value is reported here.
findings.quote: We observed that APOE4 lipid droplets showed greater co-localization with both SQSTM1/p62 and LC3B than APOE2 lipid droplets (Fig. 5O–R). This finding suggests that lipophagy in APOE4 astrocytes is impaired and cannot be activated by starvation-induced autophagy.
findings.summary: Under starvation, APOE4 lipid droplets accumulate autophagy markers more than APOE2 droplets.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE2/APOE4 human iPSC-derived astrocytes (KOLF2.1J and BIONi037)

findings.finding_description: Mass spectrometry of buoyant lipid droplet fractions found SQSTM1/p62 more abundant on APOE4 than APOE2 lipid droplets. The text calls this a trend, while the legend reports p=0.0046; the comparison for which that p-value applies is not stated.
findings.quote: Our proteomics data showed a trend that SQSTM1/p62 was more abundant on APOE4 lipid droplets than APOE2 lipid droplets (Fig. 5A).
findings.summary: The lipid droplet proteome shows more p62 on APOE4 than APOE2 droplets.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE2/3/4 human iPSC-derived astrocytes (two isogenic sets), buoyant fraction proteomics

findings.finding_description: Under prolonged starvation (5 days without media change), APOE2 astrocytes trended toward fewer lipid droplets while APOE4 astrocytes did not. This is a weak, non-significant trend; no statistics are given in the main text.
findings.quote: We observed that APOE2 astrocytes exhibited a trend towards reduced lipid droplets while APOE4 astrocytes did not (Supplementary Fig. S8Q).
findings.summary: Prolonged starvation tended to reduce lipid droplets in APOE2 but not APOE4 astrocytes (trend only).

findings.finding_description: Overrepresentation analysis of the genotype-specific lipid droplet proteomes found that proteins on APOE4 (and APOE4/APOE3-shared) but not APOE2 lipid droplets were enriched in protein secretion and autophagosome assembly pathways. This is a compositional proxy only, not a functional measure.
findings.quote: In contrast, proteins present on APOE4 lipid droplets but not found in APOE2 showed functional enrichment in protein secretion and autophagosome assembly pathways (Fig. 3B and Supplementary Data 12, 13).
findings.summary: The APOE4 lipid droplet proteome is enriched for autophagosome assembly proteins.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE2/3/4 human iPSC-derived astrocytes (two isogenic sets), buoyant fraction proteomics

findings.finding_description: Lipidomics of buoyant lipid droplet fractions showed that APOE4 droplets contained more triacylglycerol than APOE3 droplets (APOE3–APOE4 p=0.00002), while APOE3 droplets had higher cholesterol esters (Fig. 4C, APOE3–APOE4 p=0.0073). This bears on the 'APOE4 disrupts lipid metabolism vs APOE3' part of the hypothesis but measures no endolysosomal outcome. It is class 5 because neither A nor B is measured as defined: the readout is the intermediate lipid phenotype.
findings.quote: Lipid droplets from APOE3 iPSC-derived astrocytes showed high cholesterol esters, diacylglycerols and fatty acids but reduced triacylglycerols, suggesting a lower capacity to efficiently store fatty acids as triacylglycerols when stimulated with oleic acid
findings.summary: APOE4 vs APOE3 astrocytes differ in lipid droplet triacylglycerol and cholesterol ester content.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE2/3/4 human iPSC-derived astrocytes (two isogenic sets), oleic acid-treated, buoyant fraction lipidomics

findings.finding_description: APOE4 (and APOE2 and APOE-KO) iPSC-derived astrocytes accumulated more lipid droplets than APOE3 under basal conditions. This is the lipid metabolism disruption premise; genotype differences were weaker in the BIONi037 set. It is class 5 because no late endosome/lysosome readout was taken: the measure is the upstream lipid phenotype.
findings.quote: We recapitulate this finding and observe that APOE4, APOE2, and APOE-KO iPSC-derived astrocytes also accumulate lipid droplets relative to APOE3 (Supplementary Fig. S1C, D).
findings.summary: APOE4 astrocytes accumulate more lipid droplets than APOE3 astrocytes.
findings.data_location: Supplementary Fig. S1C, D; Fig. 1B, C

findings.finding_description: In post-mortem single-nucleus astrocyte transcriptomes, MAP1LC3B (LC3B) was more abundant in APOE4 than APOE2 carriers. The samples are aged and pooled AD plus control brains, so the system is outside the hypothesis's non-AD, non-aged scope; it is also a transcript-level surrogate.
findings.quote: The autophagosome marker MAP1LC3B (LC3B) was also more abundant in APOE4 compared to APOE2 carriers (Supplementary Fig. S5E).
findings.summary: Human brain astrocytes from APOE4 carriers show higher LC3B transcript levels than APOE2 carriers.
findings.experimental_system: post-mortem human frontal cortex astrocytes (snRNA-seq, AD and control)
